analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the importance of early detection and intervention to mitigate HRQoL deterioration and fatigue in HDV-infected patients.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and exclusion of treated patients limit causal inference and generalisability, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

title_zh: 慢性丁型肝炎病毒感染对健康相关生活质量和疲劳的影响:一项真实的国际研究。
source_body_en: As little is known about the disease burden of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection, this study examined health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue at different disease stages. This was a real-world quantitative cross-sectional survey of patients in Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA. Patients were recruited via their treating physicians. Patients who had received bulevirtide for hepatitis B or treatment licensed for HDV were excluded. Of 211 patients, 41% were noncirrhotic (F0-F3); 20% had liver cirrhosis with normal function (compensated); 20% had liver cirrhosis (F4) with impaired function (decompensated); 19% had hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Mean (standard deviation; SD) age was 54.5 (11.5) years, 75% were male. ANOVA showed a significant decrease (indicating poorer HRQoL) in EQ-5D-3L visual analogue scale (VAS) scores and index values with worsening disease stage and increasing severity (all p < 0.0001). All domain scores of the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 (except positive wellbeing) worsened with progressing disease and increasing symptom severity (all p ≤ 0.0001). Mean Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) total scores also increased, indicating greater fatigue, with worsening of disease and increasing symptom severity (both p < 0.0001). HDV infection significantly impacts patients' HRQoL and fatigue, particularly for patients at later disease stages. Treatments that slow disease progression, reducing the burden of HDV infection, are needed.

title: Lipid metabolism remodeling the immunological landscape of hepatocellular carcinoma: From mechanisms to therapeutics.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global malignancy with high incidence and poor survival rates. Etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions have emerged as a unifying framework for deciphering hepatocarcinogenesis. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are the two predominant etiological drivers for HCC. Although immunotherapy serves as a cornerstone of HCC treatment, therapeutic response varies considerably across distinct etiologies. Accumulating evidence suggests that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, thereby accounting for the heterogeneous responses to immunotherapy. Therefore, deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk may provide new opportunities to improve therapeutic responses. In this review, we propose the framework of etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions by comparing two major etiologies, HBV and MASLD. Moreover, taking into account the crucial role of lipid metabolism in hepatocarcinogenesis, dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies have also been included so as to offer potential therapeutic strategies.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection within the context of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), focusing on HBV as a predominant etiological driver and its role in disease pathogenesis and therapeutic response variability.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review adopts a narrative framework comparing HBV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to explore etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions, integrating dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies as potential therapeutic strategies.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV is identified as one of the two predominant etiological drivers of HCC, with accumulating evidence indicating that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, contributing to heterogeneous immunotherapy responses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights unresolved heterogeneity in immunotherapy responses across distinct etiologies, including HBV-associated HCC, without providing pooled estimates or definitive mechanistic explanations for these variations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk, particularly in HBV-associated HCC, is proposed as a priority to improve therapeutic responses, with dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies suggested as potential strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review frames hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) within an etiology-driven metabolic-immune interaction framework, identifying hepatitis B virus (HBV) as a key driver alongside metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). It synthesizes evidence that HBV-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism contributes to immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, which may underlie the variable responses to immunotherapy observed in HBV-associated HCC. The review emphasizes the need to decode these interactions to refine therapeutic strategies, proposing dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies as potential avenues. While HBV is highlighted as a predominant etiological factor, the review underscores unresolved heterogeneity in treatment responses and the lack of pooled mechanistic insights, signaling critical gaps for future research.

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了不同病因(包括 HBV 相关 HCC)免疫治疗反应中尚未解决的异质性,但没有对这些变化提供汇总估计或明确的机制解释。

analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk, particularly in HBV-associated HCC, is proposed as a priority to improve therapeutic responses, with dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies suggested as potential strategies.

title_zh: 脂质代谢重塑肝细胞癌的免疫景观:从机制到治疗。
source_body_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global malignancy with high incidence and poor survival rates. Etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions have emerged as a unifying framework for deciphering hepatocarcinogenesis. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are the two predominant etiological drivers for HCC. Although immunotherapy serves as a cornerstone of HCC treatment, therapeutic response varies considerably across distinct etiologies. Accumulating evidence suggests that etiology-specific dysregulation of lipid metabolism shapes immune imbalance in the tumor microenvironment, thereby accounting for the heterogeneous responses to immunotherapy. Therefore, deciphering etiology-driven metabolic-immune crosstalk may provide new opportunities to improve therapeutic responses. In this review, we propose the framework of etiology-driven metabolic-immune interactions by comparing two major etiologies, HBV and MASLD. Moreover, taking into account the crucial role of lipid metabolism in hepatocarcinogenesis, dietary interventions and lipid metabolism-targeted therapies have also been included so as to offer potential therapeutic strategies.
abstract_zh: 肝细胞癌(HCC)仍然是全球主要的恶性肿瘤,具有高 发病率 和低生存率。病因驱动的代谢-免疫相互作用已成为破译肝癌发生的统一框架。乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和代谢功能障碍相关的脂肪肝病 (MASLD) 是 HCC 的两个主要病因驱动因素。尽管免疫疗法是 HCC 治疗 的基石,但不同病因的治疗反应差异很大。越来越多的证据表明,脂质代谢的病因特异性失调会导致肿瘤微环境中的免疫失衡,从而解释对免疫治疗的异质反应。因此,破译病因驱动的代谢免疫串扰可能为改善治疗反应提供新的机会。在这篇综述中,我们通过比较两种主要病因(HBV 和 MASLD),提出了病因驱动的代谢-免疫相互作用的框架。此外,考虑到脂质代谢在肝癌发生中的关键作用,饮食干预和脂质代谢靶向治疗也被纳入其中,以提供潜在的治疗策略。

title: Emerging Techniques of CRISPR/Cas System in Antiviral Therapy and Diagnostics: Applications, Limitations, and Translational Perspectives.
abstract: The CRISPR/Cas (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats) system is a versatile technology for developing antiviral medicines and editing viral genomes in both diagnostics and vaccine synthesis. Emerging insights into class 2 effectors, such as Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, which target viral DNA and RNA, have revolutionized vaccines against viruses such as HIV, HPV, HBV, and EBV. Innovative diagnostic techniques such as SHERLOCK, DETECTR, and FELUDA have demonstrated system's diversity and accuracy in detecting the virus markers, supporting clinical decision-making, indicating adaptability and precision of CRISPR. This review critically evaluates CRISPR's role in RNA editing, emphasizing its importance for functional genomics and development of recombinant vaccines. Translational challenges are critically discussed, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical issues, for which unique approaches such as high-fidelity Cas variants, non-viral delivery systems, and bioethical frameworks are evaluated to address these limitations. This review also covers other social implications, such as accessibility and biosecurity risks, associated with CRISPR technologies Collectively, these advances underscore the transformative potential of CRISPR technologies in shaping next-generation antiviral diagnostics and therapeutics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the CRISPR/Cas system as a tool for antiviral therapy and diagnostics, with a focus on its potential applications against human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, including its genotypes and associated diseases such as chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis.

analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CRISPR/Cas systems, particularly Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, demonstrate versatility in antiviral applications, including genome editing and diagnostics. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies significant translational challenges, including off-target effects, delivery limitations, and ethical concerns, which remain unresolved. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of high-fidelity Cas variants and non-viral delivery systems to mitigate off-target effects and improve delivery efficiency. analysis.summary_en: This review explores the CRISPR/Cas system as a transformative tool for antiviral therapy and diagnostics, focusing on its potential against human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and associated diseases. elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了尚未解决的重大转化挑战,包括脱靶效应、交付限制和道德问题。它还指出,虽然 CRISPR 系统对 HBV 和其他病毒靶点显示出希望,但 HBV 特异性应用的证据基础尚未系统合成,并且临床环境中的长期安全性和有效性尚未确定。

title: Temporal Patterns of HBV Reactivation in Rituximab-Treated CKD Patients: An Exploratory Analysis of Baseline Quantitative HBsAg and Prophylaxis Duration.
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a severe complication in HBsAg-positive patients receiving rituximab (RTX) for chronic kidney disease (CKD). We evaluated clinical predictors of reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX. Participants were stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration: Group A (≥ 12-18 months post-RTX, n=41), Group B (6-12 months, n=47), and Group C ( Results The overall HBV reactivation was 7.6% (8/105). A significant "duration-dependent" protective effect was observed, with reactivation rates of 2.4%, 6.4%, and 23.5% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (P = 0.012). Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL (OR = 12.5, P = 0.005) and antiviral prophylaxis duration Conclusions An extended 12-18 months antiviral prophylaxis regimen provides optimal protection against HBV reactivation in CKD patients. Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL represents a noteworthy marker of heightened risk. Due to the limitations of a small event size, these findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Crucially, the observed temporal clustering between 4 and 10 months indicates a distinct post-prophylaxis risk timeline compared to non-renal populations, highlighting the need for further tailored, prospective validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients receiving rituximab (RTX) are at risk of severe Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation, yet clinical predictors and optimal antiviral prophylaxis strategies remain uncertain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective analysis included 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX, stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration into three groups: Group A (≥12–18 months, n=41), Group B (6–12 months, n=47), and Group C (<6 months, n=17).
analysis.methods: The study evaluated clinical predictors of HBV reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics using retrospective data.
analysis.main_results: Overall HBV reactivation occurred in 7.6% (8/105) of patients, with reactivation rates of 2.4% in Group A, 6.4% in Group B, and 23.5% in Group C (P=0.012). Baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL was associated with increased risk (OR=12.5, P=0.005).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that extended 12–18 months of antiviral prophylaxis provides optimal protection against HBV reactivation in CKD patients, with baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL serving as a notable risk marker.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that prolonged antiviral prophylaxis may reduce HBV reactivation risk in RTX-treated CKD patients, particularly those with high baseline HBsAg levels, warranting prospective validation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s small event size and retrospective design limit causal inference and generalizability, and the authors classify the evidence as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory retrospective study analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients treated with rituximab (RTX) to identify predictors of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation and optimal antiviral prophylaxis duration. Patients were stratified by prophylaxis duration: ≥12–18 months (n=41), 6–12 months (n=47), and <6 months (n=17). Overall HBV reactivation occurred in 7.6% (8/105), with reactivation rates of 2.4%, 6.4%, and 23.5% across the three groups, respectively (P=0.012). Baseline HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL was associated with increased risk (OR=12.5, P=0.005). The authors conclude that extended 12–18 months of prophylaxis provides optimal protection and that high baseline HBsAg levels identify patients at heightened risk. However, the small event size and retrospective design limit the strength of evidence, and the findings are exploratory.

title_zh: 利妥昔单抗治疗的 CKD 患者中 HBV 再激活的时间模式:基线定量 HBsAg 和预防持续时间的探索性分析。
source_body_en: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a severe complication in HBsAg-positive patients receiving rituximab (RTX) for chronic kidney disease (CKD). We evaluated clinical predictors of reactivation, optimal prophylaxis duration, and post-discontinuation risk kinetics. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 105 HBsAg-positive CKD patients treated with RTX. Participants were stratified by antiviral prophylaxis duration: Group A (≥ 12-18 months post-RTX, n=41), Group B (6-12 months, n=47), and Group C ( Results The overall HBV reactivation was 7.6% (8/105). A significant "duration-dependent" protective effect was observed, with reactivation rates of 2.4%, 6.4%, and 23.5% in Groups A, B, and C, respectively (P = 0.012). Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL (OR = 12.5, P = 0.005) and antiviral prophylaxis duration Conclusions An extended 12-18 months antiviral prophylaxis regimen provides optimal protection against HBV reactivation in CKD patients. Baseline HBsAg > 2.4 log10 IU/mL represents a noteworthy marker of heightened risk. Due to the limitations of a small event size, these findings remain exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Crucially, the observed temporal clustering between 4 and 10 months indicates a distinct post-prophylaxis risk timeline compared to non-renal populations, highlighting the need for further tailored, prospective validation.

analysis_zh.methods: 该研究利用回顾性数据评估了 HBV 再激活的临床预测因素、最佳预防持续时间和停药后风险动力学。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体 HBV 再激活发生率为 7.6% (8/105),其中 A 组再激活率为 2.4%,B 组为 6.4%,C 组为 23.5%(P=0.012)。基线 HBsAg >2.4 log10 IU/mL 与风险增加相关(OR=12.5,P=0.005)。

title: Seroprevalence and Early Indicators of HBV and HCV Co-infection Among Newly Diagnosed HIV Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study from India.
abstract: HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections contribute significantly to liver-associated morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (HIV/AIDS). Detection of these hepatitis co-infections at the time of HIV diagnosis is critical for the selection of the most suitable HAART regimen to improve long-term health outcomes. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 newly diagnosed, HIV-1 adult patients and screened for HBV (HBsAg) and HCV (anti-HCV) using immunoassays. Sociodemographic, behavioral, hematological, biochemical, immunological, and virological parameters were analyzed. Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for co-infections. Among all participants HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections had 3.9% and 2.5% seroprevalence respectively. Previous or present injection drug use was the best predictor, with RRR = 74.86 (95% CI 11.7-478.9, p < 0.001) for HIV-HBV and RRR = 174.67 (95% CI 22.6-1348.1, p < 0.001) for HIV-HC Non-heterosexual HIV transmission modes were also significant predictors (RRR = 8.30, 95% CI 2.2-31.2, p = 0.002 for HIV-HBV; RRR = 10.9, 2.3-52.7, HCV, p = 0.003). Compared to HIV-only patients, co-infected patients had significantly elevated bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and ALP levels, lower platelet counts and serum albumin, higher ESR, and higher HIV viral loads. Furthermore, sexual orientation (< 0.001) and substance abuse (< 0.001) significantly contribute to health risk behaviors. These findings highlights the prevalence of HBV and HCV co-infection among newly diagnosed HIV patients is lower than the global prevalence among HIV/AIDS. However, the baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators of co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening in newly diagnosed HIV patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: HIV-HBV co-infection contributes significantly to liver-associated morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV, and early detection at HIV diagnosis is critical for selecting appropriate antiretroviral therapy to improve long-term health outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 newly diagnosed, HIV-1 adult patients in India who were screened for HBV (HBsAg) and HCV (anti-HCV) using immunoassays, with sociodemographic, behavioral, hematological, biochemical, immunological, and virological parameters analyzed.
analysis.methods: Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for HBV and HCV co-infections among the participants.
analysis.main_results: HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections had seroprevalences of 3.9% and 2.5%, respectively, with previous or present injection drug use identified as the strongest predictor (RRR = 74.86 for HIV-HBV and RRR = 174.67 for HIV-HCV, both p < 0.001). Co-infected patients exhibited significantly elevated bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and ALP levels, lower platelet counts and serum albumin, higher ESR, and higher HIV viral loads compared to HIV-only patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators of HBV co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening in newly diagnosed HIV patients, and notes that the observed HBV co-infection prevalence is lower than global estimates among HIV/AIDS patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that routine HBV screening at HIV diagnosis could enable timely therapeutic decisions, particularly in populations with high-risk behaviors such as injection drug use or non-heterosexual transmission, to mitigate liver disease progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the study does not report HBV genotype distribution or long-term clinical outcomes, which constrains the generalizability and strength of evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from India assessed HBV and HCV co-infection among 282 newly diagnosed HIV-1 adult patients using immunoassays, finding seroprevalences of 3.9% for HIV-HBV and 2.5% for HIV-HCV. Injection drug use was the strongest predictor of co-infection (RRR 74.86 for HBV and 174.67 for HCV, p < 0.001), with co-infected patients showing elevated liver enzymes, lower platelet counts, and higher HIV viral loads. The authors conclude that baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators for HBV co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening at HIV diagnosis. The study acknowledges that HBV prevalence was lower than global estimates and notes limitations including the cross-sectional design and lack of genotype or long-term outcome data, warranting cautious interpretation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: HIV-HBV 合并感染对 HIV 感染者的肝脏相关发病率和 诊断 产生显着影响,而 HIV 诊断 的早期检测对于选择适当的抗逆转录病毒治疗以改善长期健康结果至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在印度 282 名新诊断的 HIV-1 成年患者中进行了一项横断面研究,这些患者使用免疫测定法筛查了 HBV (HBsAg) 和 HCV (抗 HCV),并分析了社会人口学、行为、血液学、生化、免疫学和病毒学参数。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多项逻辑回归来确定参与者中 HBV 和 HCV 合并感染的相对风险比 (RRR)。
elements_zh.main_results: HIV-HBV 和 HIV-HCV 合并感染的 血清流行率 分别为 3.9% 和 2.5%,之前或当前的注射吸毒被认为是最强的预测因子(HIV-HBV 的 RRR = 74.86,HIV-HCV 的 RRR = 174.67,均 p < 0.001)。与仅感染 HIV 的患者相比,合并感染的患者表现出显着升高的胆红素、SGOT、SGPT 和 ALP 水平、较低的血小板计数和血清白蛋白、较高的 ESR 和较高的 HIV 病毒载量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,基线实验室异常和高危行为可能作为 HBV 合并感染的早期指标,支持对新诊断的 HIV 患者进行常规肝炎筛查,并指出观察到的 HBV 合并感染 患病率 低于 HIV/AIDS 患者的全球估计值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在 HIV 诊断 进行常规 HBV 筛查可以及时做出治疗决策,特别是对于具有注射吸毒或非异性恋 传播 等高危行为的人群,以减轻肝病进展。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且该研究没有报告 HBV 基因型分布或长期临床结果,这将证据的普遍性和强度限制为中等。

analysis_en.methods: Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for HBV and HCV co-infections among the participants.
analysis_en.main_results: HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections had seroprevalences of 3.9% and 2.5%, respectively, with previous or present injection drug use identified as the strongest predictor (RRR = 74.86 for HIV-HBV and RRR = 174.67 for HIV-HCV, both p < 0.001). Co-infected patients exhibited significantly elevated bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and ALP levels, lower platelet counts and serum albumin, higher ESR, and higher HIV viral loads compared to HIV-only patients.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators of HBV co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening in newly diagnosed HIV patients, and notes that the observed HBV co-infection prevalence is lower than global estimates among HIV/AIDS patients.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that routine HBV screening at HIV diagnosis could enable timely therapeutic decisions, particularly in populations with high-risk behaviors such as injection drug use or non-heterosexual transmission, to mitigate liver disease progression.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the study does not report HBV genotype distribution or long-term clinical outcomes, which constrains the generalizability and strength of evidence to moderate.

title_zh: 血清流行率 和新诊断 HIV 患者中 HBV 和 HCV 合并感染的早期指标:来自印度的一项横断面研究。
source_body_en: HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections contribute significantly to liver-associated morbidity and mortality among people living with HIV (HIV/AIDS). Detection of these hepatitis co-infections at the time of HIV diagnosis is critical for the selection of the most suitable HAART regimen to improve long-term health outcomes. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 282 newly diagnosed, HIV-1 adult patients and screened for HBV (HBsAg) and HCV (anti-HCV) using immunoassays. Sociodemographic, behavioral, hematological, biochemical, immunological, and virological parameters were analyzed. Multinomial logistic regression was used to determine relative risk ratios (RRR) for co-infections. Among all participants HIV-HBV and HIV-HCV co-infections had 3.9% and 2.5% seroprevalence respectively. Previous or present injection drug use was the best predictor, with RRR = 74.86 (95% CI 11.7-478.9, p < 0.001) for HIV-HBV and RRR = 174.67 (95% CI 22.6-1348.1, p < 0.001) for HIV-HC Non-heterosexual HIV transmission modes were also significant predictors (RRR = 8.30, 95% CI 2.2-31.2, p = 0.002 for HIV-HBV; RRR = 10.9, 2.3-52.7, HCV, p = 0.003). Compared to HIV-only patients, co-infected patients had significantly elevated bilirubin, SGOT, SGPT, and ALP levels, lower platelet counts and serum albumin, higher ESR, and higher HIV viral loads. Furthermore, sexual orientation (< 0.001) and substance abuse (< 0.001) significantly contribute to health risk behaviors. These findings highlights the prevalence of HBV and HCV co-infection among newly diagnosed HIV patients is lower than the global prevalence among HIV/AIDS. However, the baseline laboratory abnormalities and high-risk behaviors may serve as early indicators of co-infection, supporting routine hepatitis screening in newly diagnosed HIV patients.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: HIV-HBV 合并感染对 HIV 感染者的肝脏相关发病率和 诊断 产生显着影响,而 HIV 诊断 的早期检测对于选择适当的抗逆转录病毒治疗以改善长期健康结果至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在印度 282 名新诊断的 HIV-1 成年患者中进行了一项横断面研究,这些患者使用免疫测定法筛查了 HBV (HBsAg) 和 HCV (抗 HCV),并分析了社会人口学、行为、血液学、生化、免疫学和病毒学参数。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用多项逻辑回归来确定参与者中 HBV 和 HCV 合并感染的相对风险比 (RRR)。
analysis_zh.main_results: HIV-HBV 和 HIV-HCV 合并感染的 血清流行率 分别为 3.9% 和 2.5%,之前或当前的注射吸毒被认为是最强的预测因子(HIV-HBV 的 RRR = 74.86,HIV-HCV 的 RRR = 174.67,均 p < 0.001)。与仅感染 HIV 的患者相比,合并感染的患者表现出显着升高的胆红素、SGOT、SGPT 和 ALP 水平、较低的血小板计数和血清白蛋白、较高的 ESR 和较高的 HIV 病毒载量。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,基线实验室异常和高危行为可能作为 HBV 合并感染的早期指标,支持对新诊断的 HIV 患者进行常规肝炎筛查,并指出观察到的 HBV 合并感染 患病率 低于 HIV/AIDS 患者的全球估计值。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在 HIV 诊断 进行常规 HBV 筛查可以及时做出治疗决策,特别是对于具有注射吸毒或非异性恋 传播 等高危行为的人群,以减轻肝病进展。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且该研究没有报告 HBV 基因型分布或长期临床结果,这将证据的普遍性和强度限制为中等。

title: Comparison of Factors Associated With 30-Day and 90-Day Readmission Among a Global Cohort of Patients Hospitalised With Cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: It remains unclear whether different factors influence 30- and 90-day readmission rates. We identified predictors of 90-day mortality in a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis. METHODS: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation (LT), and mortality were compared in prospectively enrolled, non-electively hospitalised adult patients with cirrhosis. RESULTS: We enrolled 4208 patients from 125 centres across 37 countries. Alcohol-related liver disease was the most common aetiology of cirrhosis (40%), followed by hepatitis B virus infection (21%); 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation (LT), and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. In multivariable analysis, country income was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission rates, the receipt of LT, and mortality within 30 and 90 days post-discharge (all p-values < 0.001). Independent predictors of higher rates of 30- and 90-day readmissions, respectively, were disease severity (p < 0.001, p = 0.003), prior ascites (p = 0.025, p = 0.016), prior hospitalisation (p < 0.001), hyponatremia (p < 0.001, p = 0.008), and in-hospital vasopressor use (p = 0.002, p = 0.011). Prior variceal bleeding independently predicted higher 90-day readmission rates, whereas age, disease severity, mechanical ventilation, and in-hospital vasopressor use (all, p < 0.001) increased odds of 30- and 90-day post-discharge death. Additionally, admission (p = 0.011) and nosocomial (p = 0.022) infections increased the odds of 90-day post-discharge death. CONCLUSION: In a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis, patients in high-income countries exhibited the highest rates of 30- and 90-day readmission, alongside lower mortality rates and a higher incidence of LT. Variables that predict 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission. Understanding these disparities is essential for achieving health equity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unresolved question of whether distinct clinical or demographic factors differentially influence 30-day versus 90-day hospital readmission among patients hospitalised with cirrhosis globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a prospective, multicentre, non-elective cohort study enrolling 4208 adult patients with cirrhosis across 125 centres in 37 countries.
analysis.methods: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality were compared using multivariable analyses to identify independent predictors.
analysis.main_results: Among 4208 patients, 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation, and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. Country income level was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission, transplantation, and mortality (all p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that predictors of 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission, highlighting shared risk factors across time horizons and disparities linked to country income levels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted interventions addressing disease severity, prior ascites, hyponatremia, and infection control may reduce early and late readmissions, particularly in lower-income settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s abstract-only evidence limits detailed assessment of methodological rigor, potential biases, and generalisability beyond hospitalised cirrhosis populations, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This global prospective cohort study of 4208 hospitalised adults with cirrhosis identified shared predictors for 30- and 90-day readmission, including disease severity, prior ascites, prior hospitalisation, hyponatremia, and in-hospital vasopressor use. Country income level was significantly associated with readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality within both time frames. Alcohol-related liver disease accounted for 40% of cirrhosis aetiologies, and 47% of patients were readmitted within 90 days. The authors emphasise that variables predicting early readmission also predict later readmission, underscoring the need for equitable health strategies to address disparities linked to socioeconomic factors.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项前瞻性、多中心、非选择性 队列研究 研究,招募了 37 个国家 125 个中心的 4208 名成年肝硬化患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多变量分析比较与出院后 30 天和 90 天再入院、肝移植和 死亡率 相关的变量,以确定独立的预测因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在4208名患者中,47%再次入院,8%接受肝移植,23%在出院后90天内死亡。国家收入水平与 30 天和 90 天再入院、移植和 死亡率 显着相关(所有 p < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,30 天再入院的预测因素也预测了 90 天再入院的情况,强调了不同时间范围内的共同风险因素以及与国家收入水平相关的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对疾病严重程度、既往腹水、低钠血症和感染控制的针对性干预措施可能会减少早期和晚期再入院,特别是在低收入环境中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的仅抽象证据限制了对方法严谨性、潜在偏差和住院肝硬化人群之外的普遍性的详细评估,需要适度的信心。

abstract_zh: 背景和目的:尚不清楚不同因素是否影响 30 天和 90 天的再入院率。我们在肝硬化住院患者的全球 队列研究 中确定了 90 天 死亡率 的预测因子。方法:在前瞻性入组、非选择性住院的成年肝硬化患者中,比较与出院后 30 天和 90 天再入院、肝移植 (LT) 和 死亡率 相关的变量。结果:我们招募了来自 37 个国家 125 个中心的 4208 名患者。酒精相关性肝病是肝硬化最常见的病因(40%),其次是 乙型肝炎病毒 感染(21%);47% 的患者再次入院,8% 的患者接受肝移植 (LT),23% 的患者在出院后 90 天内死亡。在多变量分析中,国家收入与 30 天和 90 天的再入院率、LT 的接受情况以及出院后 30 和 90 天内的 死亡率 显着相关(所有 p 值 < 0.001)。30 天和 90 天再入院率较高的独立预测因素分别是疾病严重程度 (p < 0.001,p = 0.003)、既往腹水 (p = 0.025,p = 0.016)、既往住院情况 (p < 0.001)、低钠血症 (p < 0.001,p = 0.008) 和住院情况血管加压药的使用(p = 0.002,p = 0.011)。既往静脉曲张出血独立预测较高的 90 天再入院率,而年龄、疾病严重程度、机械通气和院内血管加压药的使用(全部,p < 0.001)增加出院后 30 天和 90 天的死亡几率。此外,入院感染 (p = 0.011) 和院内感染 (p = 0.022) 会增加出院后 90 天的死亡几率。结论:在全球肝硬化住院患者 队列研究 中,高收入国家患者的 30 天和 90 天再入院率最高,同时 死亡率 率较低,LT 发病率 较高。预测 30 天再入院的变量也预测 90 天再入院。了解这些差异对于实现健康公平至关重要。

title: Metagenomic sequencing detects viruses and bacteria in a cross-sectional clinical cohort of undifferentiated febrile illness in Nigeria
abstract: UNLABELLED: Molecular and microscopy-based diagnostic capacity is often insufficient or unavailable in places where infectious disease burdens are highest, such as in West Africa. Rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) can provide quick and affordable diagnoses of common infections but is an imperfect solution due to limitations around detecting and dealing with false-negative and false-positive results. An alternative to RDT is unbiased metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance. Here, we present data from unbiased metagenomic sequencing used to identify causes of undiagnosed febrile illness in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Proof of concept for this approach has been demonstrated by several groups who have identified epidemic and endemic viral diseases like Lassa fever, yellow fever, and chikungunya. We show that unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis can be used to identify RNA viruses in clinical samples. We sequenced RNA from sera of patients (n = 343), many of whom were acutely febrile (76%), in a survey of clinics in Jos. We detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11 %) specimens. Among these were hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most of the viruses identified are unlikely to cause clinical symptoms in the patients we sampled, their presence demonstrates the validity of our approach. Additionally, our sequencing data allowed us to identify genetic material from potentially pathogenic bacteria, another possible etiological agent of febrile illness. IMPORTANCE: In low-resource areas, fevers due to infectious pathogens are a major source of illness, but tools for detecting and identifying such pathogens are often limited. Unbiased approaches for identifying genetic material from all potentially infectious organisms in a sample represent an opportunity for discovering sources of fever. Metagenomic sequencing can improve insight into pathogen landscapes in low-resource settings, potentially providing early detection of disease outbreaks. However, unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) is no panacea; it is susceptible to contamination and false positives. We used mNGS to evaluate serum from >300 Nigerian clinic-goers in Jos, Nigeria, most of whom (>70%) had fevers of unknown origin. Our goal was to understand arbovirus prevalence in Jos, Nigeria, and identify the sources of infection not routinely monitored for at clinics. We detected hepatitis B virus, as well as nonpathogenic anelloviruses. Our study provides insight into the utility and limitations of mNGS for pathogen surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of current diagnostic tools in low-resource settings by exploring the utility of metagenomic sequencing for identifying pathogens in febrile illness cases. The background highlights the insufficient diagnostic capacity in West Africa, where infectious fevers are prevalent but difficult to diagnose.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, involving 343 patients, many of whom had fevers of unknown origin. The study focused on clinical samples from these patients to evaluate the effectiveness of metagenomic sequencing in pathogen detection.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed unbiased metagenomic sequencing to analyze RNA from serum samples of patients. This approach allowed them to identify both viral and bacterial genetic material, including potential pathogens associated with febrile illness.
analysis.main_results: Five human-infecting viruses were detected in 11% of the specimens, including hepatitis B virus and several anelloviruses. The presence of these viruses, even if not causing symptoms, demonstrated the feasibility of the metagenomic sequencing approach.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides evidence that metagenomic sequencing can effectively identify pathogens in clinical samples, even in low-resource settings. This approach offers a new tool for understanding the pathogen landscape and detecting emerging diseases.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that metagenomic sequencing can enhance pathogen surveillance and improve the identification of infectious causes of fever, which is critical for public health responses in regions with limited diagnostic resources.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the limitations of metagenomic sequencing, such as susceptibility to contamination and false positives, but presents a high-confidence approach for pathogen detection in clinical samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the use of metagenomic sequencing to identify pathogens in patients with undifferentiated febrile illness in Nigeria. The research highlights the limitations of traditional diagnostic methods in low-resource settings and demonstrates the potential of unbiased sequencing to detect both viral and bacterial agents. Five human-infecting viruses, including hepatitis B virus, were identified in 11% of the specimens, showcasing the feasibility of this approach. The study emphasizes the importance of metagenomic sequencing for improving pathogen surveillance and understanding the etiology of febrile illnesses. However, it also notes the challenges of contamination and false positives associated with this method. The findings suggest that this technique could be a valuable tool for identifying infectious causes of fever in resource-limited areas, contributing to better public health strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究在尼日利亚高原州乔斯进行,涉及 343 名患者,其中许多人出现不明原因发烧。该研究重点关注这些患者的临床样本,以评估宏基因组测序在病原体检测中的有效性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员采用无偏倚的宏基因组测序来分析患者血清样本中的 RNA。这种方法使他们能够识别病毒和细菌遗传物质,包括与发热性疾病相关的潜在病原体。
elements_zh.main_results: 11%的样本中检测到五种人类感染病毒,包括乙型肝炎病毒和几种指环病毒。这些病毒的存在,即使不会引起症状,也证明了宏基因组测序方法的可行性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of current diagnostic tools in low-resource settings by exploring the utility of metagenomic sequencing for identifying pathogens in febrile illness cases. The background highlights the insufficient diagnostic capacity in West Africa, where infectious fevers are prevalent but difficult to diagnose.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria, involving 343 patients, many of whom had fevers of unknown origin. The study focused on clinical samples from these patients to evaluate the effectiveness of metagenomic sequencing in pathogen detection.
analysis_en.methods: The researchers employed unbiased metagenomic sequencing to analyze RNA from serum samples of patients. This approach allowed them to identify both viral and bacterial genetic material, including potential pathogens associated with febrile illness.
analysis_en.main_results: Five human-infecting viruses were detected in 11% of the specimens, including hepatitis B virus and several anelloviruses. The presence of these viruses, even if not causing symptoms, demonstrated the feasibility of the metagenomic sequencing approach.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study provides evidence that metagenomic sequencing can effectively identify pathogens in clinical samples, even in low-resource settings. This approach offers a new tool for understanding the pathogen landscape and detecting emerging diseases.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that metagenomic sequencing can enhance pathogen surveillance and improve the identification of infectious causes of fever, which is critical for public health responses in regions with limited diagnostic resources.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges the limitations of metagenomic sequencing, such as susceptibility to contamination and false positives, but presents a high-confidence approach for pathogen detection in clinical samples.

title_zh: 宏基因组测序在尼日利亚未分化发热性疾病的横断面临床 队列研究 中检测到病毒和细菌
source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Molecular and microscopy-based diagnostic capacity is often insufficient or unavailable in places where infectious disease burdens are highest, such as in West Africa. Rapid diagnostic testing (RDT) can provide quick and affordable diagnoses of common infections but is an imperfect solution due to limitations around detecting and dealing with false-negative and false-positive results. An alternative to RDT is unbiased metagenomic sequencing for pathogen surveillance. Here, we present data from unbiased metagenomic sequencing used to identify causes of undiagnosed febrile illness in Jos, Plateau State, Nigeria. Proof of concept for this approach has been demonstrated by several groups who have identified epidemic and endemic viral diseases like Lassa fever, yellow fever, and chikungunya. We show that unbiased deep sequencing and metagenomic analysis can be used to identify RNA viruses in clinical samples. We sequenced RNA from sera of patients (n = 343), many of whom were acutely febrile (76%), in a survey of clinics in Jos. We detected five human-infecting viruses in 39 (11 %) specimens. Among these were hepatitis B virus, human pegivirus, and several anelloviruses. While most of the viruses identified are unlikely to cause clinical symptoms in the patients we sampled, their presence demonstrates the validity of our approach. Additionally, our sequencing data allowed us to identify genetic material from potentially pathogenic bacteria, another possible etiological agent of febrile illness. IMPORTANCE: In low-resource areas, fevers due to infectious pathogens are a major source of illness, but tools for detecting and identifying such pathogens are often limited. Unbiased approaches for identifying genetic material from all potentially infectious organisms in a sample represent an opportunity for discovering sources of fever. Metagenomic sequencing can improve insight into pathogen landscapes in low-resource settings, potentially providing early detection of disease outbreaks. However, unbiased metagenomic sequencing (mNGS) is no panacea; it is susceptible to contamination and false positives. We used mNGS to evaluate serum from >300 Nigerian clinic-goers in Jos, Nigeria, most of whom (>70%) had fevers of unknown origin. Our goal was to understand arbovirus prevalence in Jos, Nigeria, and identify the sources of infection not routinely monitored for at clinics. We detected hepatitis B virus, as well as nonpathogenic anelloviruses. Our study provides insight into the utility and limitations of mNGS for pathogen surveillance.

title: Viral coinfections and checkpoint-marker expression in HIV: An exploratory HCV-Related CD4+ T-Cell PD-L1 pattern
abstract: Chronic viral coinfections may contribute to persistent immune dysregulation in people with HIV, but their association with PD-1/PD-L1 expression remains uncertain. We analysed 100 people with HIV using available-case endpoint analyses and marker-specific paired baseline-to-follow-up analyses. Follow-up was scheduled at 12 months (allowable window, 9–15 months), and all participants had HIV RNA < 50 copies/mL at the endpoint. Baseline HBV contact, HCV status, and CMV IgG serostatus were evaluated in relation to PD-1 and PD-L1 expression on CD4+ T cells and CD19+ B cells and exploratory composite checkpoint-expression indices. HBV contact and CMV IgG serostatus were not associated with reproducible differences. The global comparison of longitudinal CD4+ T-cell PD-L1 change across HCV groups did not remain significant after false-discovery-rate correction; an exploratory pairwise comparison suggested a greater increase in participants with baseline HCV RNA positivity. Overall, the HCV-related pattern was hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

title: Toward Robust Characterization of Dynamic Binding Pockets: Lessons from the HBV Capsid Assembly Modulator Site
abstract: Abstract Protein function often depends on ligand binding pockets that fluctuate among conformational states, altering their size, shape, topology, and accessibility, yet quantitative comparison of these dynamic cavities remains challenging because their boundaries are often inherently ambiguous. The measure volinterior algorithm uses fuzzy-boundary detection to characterize enclosed molecular spaces; here, the hepatitis B virus (HBV) capsid assembly modulator (CAM) binding site is used as a model system to develop and validate a practical workflow for applying the method to dynamic protein binding pockets. The resulting methodology provides practical guidance for parameter selection and evaluation, establishes a standardized protocol for quantitative characterization of the HBV CAM pocket, and demonstrates robust, reproducible performance across conformational ensembles derived from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. More broadly, this work provides a reproducible strategy for adapting measure volinterior to other dynamic binding pockets, enabling consistent comparison of pocket geometry among independent structural studies.

The resulting methodology provides practical guidance for parameter selection and evaluation, establishes a standardized protocol for quantitative characterization of the HBV CAM pocket, and demonstrates robust, reproducible performance across conformational ensembles derived from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. More broadly, this work provides a reproducible strategy for adapting measure volinterior to other dynamic binding pockets, enabling consistent comparison of pocket geometry among independent structural studies.

title: Solitary Peritoneal Metastasis of AFP-Negative Hepatocellular Carcinoma in a 65-Year-Old Man with a History of Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy. Peritoneal metastasis is uncommon but carries a poor prognosis. Diagnosis of HCC with peritoneal metastasis is particularly challenging when alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels are normal. This report highlights diagnostic difficulties and the critical role of histopathological confirmation in such atypical presentations. CASE REPORT A 65-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and a history of lung adenocarcinoma, who had previously undergone radiofrequency ablation and partial hepatectomy for HCC (the primary tumor was histologically confirmed as moderately differentiated HCC with negative AFP immunostaining), presented with recurrent left lower abdominal pain. Laboratory tests showed normal serum AFP but elevated carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125). Imaging revealed a solitary peritoneal mass without evidence of intrahepatic recurrence. The patient underwent surgical resection. Immunohistochemistry confirmed hepatocellular origin (hepatocyte paraffin 1-positive, arginase-1-positive) and excluded lung adenocarcinoma (thyroid transcription factor-1-negative, napsin A-negative). Importantly, AFP immunohistochemistry findings were negative in the metastatic tumor, consistent with the primary tumor. The Ki-67 proliferation index was 50%. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and no recurrence was observed at the 3-month follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Normal AFP levels do not exclude recurrent or metastatic HCC. In patients with multiple primary malignancies, diagnosis of new lesions requires careful integration of clinical history, imaging findings, and histopathological evaluation. Surgery may offer both diagnostic and therapeutic value in selected patients, although its long-term benefit remains uncertain.

title: Oncoviruses at the Crossroads of Ageing and Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms and Key Signalling Pathways.
abstract: Oncoviruses are responsible for a substantial fraction of human cancers and have emerged as critical modulators of host cellular pathways that also govern ageing. The convergence of viral oncogenesis, ageing, and cancer reflects shared molecular mechanisms, including genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. Increasing evidence indicates that oncoviruses such as human papillomavirus, Epstein-Barr virus, hepatitis B and C viruses, and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus actively reprogramme host signalling networks to promote persistent infection, immune evasion, and malignant transformation. This review synthesises current knowledge on how oncoviruses intersect with key hallmarks of ageing and cancer, with particular emphasis on the signalling pathways that bridge these processes. Central pathways, including p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, are frequently targeted by viral proteins, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions not only facilitate tumourigenesis but also accelerate ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, such as immunosenescence and inflammaging. Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The scope examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and its disease manifestations, including chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis. The central question addresses how HBV intersects with host cellular pathways linked to ageing and cancer, focusing on shared molecular mechanisms and signalling networks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis that integrates current knowledge on oncoviruses, ageing, and cancer without specifying databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or selection methods. It does not report an included-study count, meta-analysis, or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HBV, alongside other oncoviruses, actively reprograms host signalling pathways such as p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin, leading to dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence. These interactions contribute to both tumourigenesis and ageing-associated cellular dysfunctions, including immunosenescence and inflammaging.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not provide target-specific evidence on HBV genotypes or detailed mechanistic studies linking HBV to ageing pathways. It lacks discussion of heterogeneity across HBV genotypes, populations, or regions, and does not address unresolved mechanisms specific to HBV.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need to elucidate HBV-specific mechanisms that bridge ageing and cancer to identify novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating HBV-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines human hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and its disease outcomes, including chronic hepatitis B, acute hepatitis B, HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma, and HBV-related cirrhosis. It explores how HBV intersects with host cellular pathways linked to ageing and cancer, focusing on shared mechanisms such as genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, telomere attrition, and chronic inflammation. The review concludes that HBV reprograms key signalling pathways (p53, mTOR, NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, Wnt/β-catenin), driving dysregulated cell survival, proliferation, and senescence, while also contributing to immunosenescence and inflammaging. However, the review lacks target-specific evidence on HBV genotypes, mechanistic heterogeneity, or unresolved mechanisms, and does not provide detailed implications for surveillance, diagnosis, or treatment specific to HBV.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该范围检查人类 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染及其疾病表现,包括 慢性乙型肝炎、急性乙型肝炎、HBV 相关肝细胞癌和 HBV 相关肝硬化。核心问题涉及 HBV 如何与与衰老和癌症相关的 宿主 细胞通路交叉,重点关注共享的分子机制和信号网络。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一种叙述性综合,整合了有关肿瘤病毒、衰老和癌症的当前知识,没有指定数据库、搜索日期、资格标准或选择方法。它不报告纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,HBV 与其他肿瘤病毒一样,主动重新编程 宿主 信号通路,例如 p53、mTOR、NF-κB、PI3K/AKT 和 Wnt/β-连环蛋白,导致细胞存活、增殖和衰老失调。这些相互作用会导致肿瘤发生和衰老相关的细胞功能障碍,包括免疫衰老和炎症。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有提供有关 HBV 基因型的特定目标证据,也没有提供将 HBV 与衰老途径联系起来的详细机制研究。它缺乏对 HBV 基因型、人群或地区异质性的讨论,也没有解决 HBV 特有的未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要阐明连接衰老和癌症的 HBV 特异性机制,以确定预防和治疗老龄化人群中 HBV 相关恶性肿瘤的新治疗靶点和策略。

Furthermore, we discuss how virus-induced modulation of the tumour microenvironment and host immune responses contributes to the dynamic interplay between ageing and cancer. Understanding these interconnected pathways provides valuable insights into the dual role of oncoviruses as drivers of both age-related decline and cancer development. Elucidating these mechanisms may reveal novel therapeutic targets and strategies for preventing and treating virus-associated malignancies in ageing populations.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是一种叙述性综合,整合了有关肿瘤病毒、衰老和癌症的当前知识,没有指定数据库、搜索日期、资格标准或选择方法。它不报告纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。

title: A new role of class A HBV capsid assembly modulators in core protein dynamics and cccDNA replenishment.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Current treatments of chronic hepatitis B are rarely curative. Capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) target capsid formation by the hepatitis B virus (HBV) core protein. Class A CAMs (CAM-A) induce abnormal core protein assembly but how they affect core protein dynamics and inhibit HBV replication is only partially understood. METHODS: Human liver chimeric mice and HBV-susceptible cells were infected to monitor dynamic changes and the fate of core protein and assembled capsids. We analyzed HBV virus and protein dynamics over four weeks under treatment of CAM-A molecule HAP_R01. RESULTS: We found an altered nuclear-cytoplasmic distribution of HBV core protein upon treatment with HAP_R01. This effect was confirmed in primary human hepatocytes and in HBV-infected liver-humanized mice. Mechanism-of-action studies in HBV-permissive cells demonstrated that HAP_R01 primarily targets newly synthesized core protein and affects capsid assembly, core protein localization and solubility in a dose- and time-dependent manner. At 50 nM, HAP_R01 promoted assembly of HBV genome-free capsids and nuclear accumulation of core protein. At ≥500 nM, HAP_R01 treatment reduced soluble core protein and capsid levels, but markedly increased insoluble core protein levels, resulting in an overall intracellular accumulation of core protein. Insoluble nuclear agglomerations of core protein were deposited in promyelocytic leukemia nuclear bodies. Treating infected cells for 31 days significantly reduced an established covalently closed circular (ccc)DNA pool and secreted HBsAg and HBeAg levels, by inhibiting cccDNA replenishment. CONCLUSIONS: As an exemplary CAM-A, HAP_R01 inhibits HBV genome replication by perturbing capsid assembly and by inducing insoluble core protein accumulation in the nucleus that affects replenishment of the cccDNA pool.
journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology

title: Prevalence and control strategies of blood-borne occupational exposures among healthcare workers in Shaoxing Second Hospital from 2020 to 2025.
abstract: ObjectiveTo analyze the characteristics and risk factors of blood-borne occupational exposures among healthcare workers at Shaoxing Second Hospital from 2020 to 2025 and to inform targeted prevention and control strategies.MethodsA retrospective analysis was performed on 252 blood-borne occupational exposure events reported from January 2020 to December 2025. Occupational distribution, occurrence patterns, exposure routes, high-risk operations, pathogens, and postexposure prophylaxis data were statistically analyzed.ResultsThe annual standardized incidence of blood-borne occupational exposures increased year by year. Nurses and staff with <5 years of service were the highest-risk groups. Sharp instrument injuries accounted for 92.46% of exposures. Hepatitis B virus was the dominant known pathogen (25.78%), whereas the hepatitis B virus postexposure prophylaxis rate was only 21.21%.ConclusionsThese findings indicate that healthcare workers at this hospital exhibit distinct high-risk features for blood-borne occupational exposures. To mitigate occupational exposure risks, a systematic and precise prevention program, hierarchical management of high-risk groups, and regular hepatitis B virus immune monitoring are recommended.
journal: The Journal of international medical research

title: Current hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) status in Pakistan: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary liver cancer and the sixth leading cause of death worldwide. HCC incidence numbers are constantly increasing in Pakistan and are mainly caused by chronic HBV and HCV associated cirrhosis. Two Pakistani population-based studies reported that the frequency of HCV induced HCC was high compared to HBV and alcohol-induced HCC. In Pakistan, the reported incidence of alcohol-induced HCC is very low. Therefore, the number of alcohol-induced HCC cases is deficient. Literature was searched using ScienceDirect, PubMed, Google Scholar, Springer, and BMC. Pakistani population studies based on HBV induced HCC, HCV induced HCC, HBV + HCV co-infection induced HCC, and alcohol induced HCC were included. A total of 98 studies on HCC were included; among them, 32 were related to HCV induced HCC, 20 were related to HBV induced HCC, 20 were associated with HBV + HCV co-infection induced HCC, and 6 were related to alcohol induced HCC. We further investigated that surgery and radiotherapy are the primary treatments for HCC in Pakistan, with surgery being the most frequently applied treatment in 1820 cases. We conducted this systematic review to highlight the current status of HCC in Pakistan. We found that HCC is most commonly caused by HCV infection compared to HBV infection and alcoholism.

title: Diverging trends and persistent inequities in cirrhosis burden across sub-Saharan Africa: projections to 2040.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Liver cirrhosis and chronic liver diseases remain major causes of premature mortality globally, with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). We aimed to quantify temporal trends and future projections of cirrhosis burden in SSA and assess the potential impact of hepatitis B vaccination scale-up. METHODS: We analysed Global Burden of Disease 2023 data from 1990 to 2023. Age-standardised death rates (ASDRs) and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were examined by sex, geography, aetiology, and socio-demographic index (SDI). Bayesian hierarchical models were used to project burden to 2040, including a scenario-based hepatitis B vaccination intervention. RESULTS: In 2023, cirrhosis accounted for 179,329 deaths in SSA, despite a 31% decline in ASDR since 1990. Absolute deaths increased by 72%, and DALYs rose by 68%, reflecting demographic change. Hepatitis B (37%), hepatitis C (29%), and alcohol-related cirrhosis (14%) were the leading causes. Marked geographic and sex disparities persisted, with the highest burden in Central and Western SSA and among males. title: Decoding Tumor Heterogeneity with Imaging Biomarkers Predicts Microvascular Invasion and Postoperative Risk Stratification in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a major driver of recurrence and poor outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet biopsy-based pathologic assessment is invasive and susceptible to sampling bias and delayed availability. We aimed to develop and validate a noninvasive preoperative model integrating multiphase magnetic resonance imaging-derived habitat/intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) features and clinical variables for MVI prediction and postoperative recurrence-risk stratification. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 978 patients with HCC from four tertiary centers. Seven models were constructed: four unimodal, two bimodal, and one trimodal (Decision). Model performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration, and decision curve analysis in the internal and external validation cohorts. Prognostic value for recurrence-free survival (RFS) was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis, and compared with clinicopathologic risk stratification. Subgroup analyses stratified by hepatitis B virus (HBV) status and histologic differentiation were used to assess robustness. RESULTS: The decision model achieved AUCs of 0.912, 0.875, and 0.882 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, and significantly outperformed the clinical model, all unimodal models, and the Rad-Clinical model (p < 0.001). Model ablation analyses demonstrated incremental gains from incorporating clinical variables with imaging features and from jointly modeling subregional composition using habitat phenotyping and ITH metrics. In the external validation cohort, the model outperformed the clinicopathologic model for recurrence-risk stratification, with a higher C-index (0.776 vs. 0.702) and higher AUCs at 2 years (0.810 vs. 0.729) and 5 years (0.876 vs. Performance was consistent across HBV- and histologic grade-based subgroups. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis supported model interpretability. CONCLUSION: The preoperative decision model demonstrated robust performance for MVI prediction and postoperative recurrence-risk stratification, supporting its potential role as an adjunct tool for preoperative risk assessment.

title: Oncogenic Viruses and Human Cancer: Molecular Mechanisms, Diagnostics, Vaccines and Therapeutic Advances
abstract: Oncogenic viruses are preventable or therapeutically tractable causes of a substantial and geographically unequal fraction of human cancer.Their biological diversity, from small DNA viruses to retroviruses and non-integrating RNA viruses, has produced distinct tumour phenotypes but also revealed recurrent principles of carcinogenesis.This critical narrative review integrates evidence on high-risk human papillomaviruses, hepatitis B, C, and D viruses, Epstein-Barr virus, Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, human T-cell leukaemia virus type 1, and Merkel cell polyomavirus.Human immunodeficiency virus is considered as an indirect carcinogenic cofactor through immune dysregulation, whereas human cytomegalovirus is treated as an unresolved candidate rather than an established tumour virus.Literature indexed through 2 June 2026 was selected from biomedical and scholarly databases, authoritative institutional sources, citation tracing, and DOI registries, with emphasis on causal evidence, mechanistic coherence, clinical validity, and translational relevance.The strongest shared mechanisms are persistent infection, dysregulated viral gene expression, interference with tumour suppressor and cell-cycle control, genomic or epigenomic instability, chronic inflammation, and immune escape.Yet the relative contribution of these processes differs markedly by virus, Review Articletissue, host immunity, and co-exposure.Diagnostics are most mature where viral biomarkers define tumour aetiology or enable screening, notably high-risk human papillomavirus testing, Epstein-Barr virus DNA in endemic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and viral oncoprotein antibodies in selected Merkel cell carcinoma settings.Prophylactic vaccination has generated the clearest cancer-prevention evidence for human papillomavirus and hepatitis B virus, while elimination barriers, incomplete coverage, persistent post-cure risk, and the absence of licensed vaccines for several tumour viruses limit population impact.Immune checkpoint blockade and virus-specific cellular therapies demonstrate that viral antigens can be clinically actionable, but response heterogeneity and implementation complexity remain substantial.Progress now depends on harmonised viral attribution, prospective biomarker validation, prevention programmes designed for equity, and trials that integrate viral biology with tumour genomics and host immunity.

title: Stimulation of the STING pathway leads to inhibition of HBV replication: insights into the role of hepatic macrophages.
abstract: Abstract Background Activation of the host immune system is a promising strategy for treating hepatitis B (HBV). The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway acts as an innate immune sensor for viral DNA. We aimed to determine whether STING activation can inhibit HBV replication in the liver. Methods We evaluated STING expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and liver biopsy specimens from patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). We examined the effect of the STING agonist DMXAA on HBV replication and the immune response in a mouse model with persistent HBV replication (rAAV8-HBV1.3). Additionally, we depleted macrophages in vivo to assess their role in DMXAA’s antiviral effects. Results STING expression in CHB patients was higher in the immune-active phase than in the inactive phase or uninfected healthy controls, suggesting an association between elevated STING expression and immune activation. In a mouse model with persistent HBV replication, DMXAA reduced serum HBV DNA in a dose-dependent manner, whereas repeated administration reduced serum HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels and enhanced hepatic immune responses. Transcriptome sequencing of liver tissues revealed 856 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in immune-related signaling pathways. In hepatic macrophage-depleted mice, the reductions in HBV virological markers following DMXAA treatment were less pronounced. Conclusions STING pathway activation enhances the immune response against HBV by upregulating the expression of immune-related genes. Hepatic macrophages play an important role in STING-mediated inhibition of HBV replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of activating the STING pathway to inhibit HBV replication. abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 激活 宿主 免疫系统是治疗乙型肝炎 (HBV) 的一种有前景的策略。干扰素基因刺激剂 (STING) 信号通路充当病毒 DNA 的先天免疫传感器。我们的目的是确定 STING 激活是否可以抑制肝脏中的 HBV 复制。方法 我们评估了 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者外周血单核细胞 (PBMC) 和肝活检标本中 STING 的表达。我们在具有持续 HBV 复制的小鼠模型 (rAAV8-HBV1.3) 中检查了 STING 激动剂 DMXAA 对 HBV 复制和 免疫应答 的影响。此外,我们还耗尽了体内巨噬细胞,以评估它们在 DMXAA 的 抗病毒药物 效应中的作用。结果 CHB 患者的 STING 表达在免疫活跃期高于非活跃期或未感染的健康对照,表明 STING 表达升高与免疫激活之间存在关联。在持续 HBV 复制的小鼠模型中,DMXAA 以剂量依赖性方式降低血清 HBV DNA,而重复给药则降低血清 HBV DNA、HBsAg 和 HBeAg 水平,并增强肝脏 免疫应答。肝组织的转录组测序揭示了涉及免疫相关信号通路的 856 个差异表达基因 (DEG)。在肝巨噬细胞耗尽的小鼠中,DMXAA 治疗 后 HBV 病毒学标志物的降低不太明显。结论 STING 通路激活通过上调免疫相关基因的表达增强 免疫应答 抗 HBV 的能力。肝巨噬细胞在 STING 介导的 HBV 复制抑制中发挥重要作用。

title: HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels at year 6 do not predict HCC risk in patients with cirrhosis on long-term entecavir therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The prognostic value of on-treatment hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA, hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg), and quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains uncertain. We evaluate the predictive roles of these viral markers in patients with CHB receiving long-term entecavir therapy. METHODS: This prospective, multicenter study enrolled patients with CHB-related cirrhosis undergoing long-term entecavir treatment and HCC surveillance in Taiwan. Serum HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were measured at enrollment. Multivariable regression identified predictors of HBV RNA positivity and HCC development. RESULTS: Overall, 451 patients were included. After a median of 6.2 years of antiviral therapy, the median levels of HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg were 0.9 log10 copies/mL, 3.2 log10 U/mL, and 2.4 log10 IU/mL, respectively. During a median 3.3-year follow-up, 55 developed HCC. 57.2% of patients had detectable HBV RNA. HBV RNA detectability was associated with older age, lower alanine aminotransferase (ALT), HBeAg positivity, and higher HBsAg and HBcrAg levels. In multivariable analysis, higher fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [aSHR], 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.00-1.21) and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) (aSHR, 1.01; 95% CI 1.00-1.01) independently predicted HCC development, whereas the three viral markers did not. CONCLUSION: After a 6-year entecavir therapy, 57.2% of patients with CHB-related cirrhosis had detectable HBV RNA. Year-6 HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were not predictive of HCC, while FIB-4 index and AFP remained independent predictors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The prognostic value of on-treatment hepatitis B virus (HBV) RNA, hepatitis B core-related antigen (HBcrAg), and quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains uncertain, creating a knowledge gap regarding their utility in risk stratification.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective, multicenter study enrolled patients with CHB-related cirrhosis undergoing long-term entecavir treatment and HCC surveillance in Taiwan, with serum viral markers measured at enrollment.
analysis.methods: Serum HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were measured at enrollment, and multivariable regression identified predictors of HBV RNA positivity and HCC development.
analysis.main_results: Among 451 patients, after a median 6.2 years of therapy, median HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels were 0.9 log10 copies/mL, 3.2 log10 U/mL, and 2.4 log10 IU/mL, respectively; 55 developed HCC during a median 3.3-year follow-up, and multivariable analysis showed that higher FIB-4 index and elevated AFP independently predicted HCC, whereas the three viral markers did not.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that year-6 HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels are not predictive of HCC risk in patients with CHB-related cirrhosis on long-term entecavir therapy, highlighting the continued relevance of FIB-4 and AFP as predictors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that routine monitoring of HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg may not improve HCC risk prediction in this population, supporting continued reliance on established clinical and laboratory markers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and single-country setting, which may restrict generalizability, and the evidence is assessed as moderate due to the absence of target-specific randomized comparisons and potential residual confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective multicenter study in Taiwan evaluated whether on-treatment HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg levels predict hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in 451 patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB)-related cirrhosis receiving long-term entecavir therapy. After a median 6.2 years of antiviral treatment, median viral marker levels were low, and 55 patients developed HCC during a median 3.3-year follow-up. Multivariable analysis showed that higher fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) independently predicted HCC, whereas HBV RNA, HBcrAg, and HBsAg did not. The authors conclude that these viral markers measured at year 6 are not predictive of HCC risk in this population, reinforcing the value of established clinical predictors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 治疗 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) RNA、乙型肝炎核心相关抗原 (HBcrAg) 和定量乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 对 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者肝细胞癌 (HCC) 风险的预后价值仍不确定,这造成了关于它们在风险分层中的实用性的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项前瞻性、多中心研究在台湾入组了接受长期恩替卡韦 治疗 和 HCC 监测 治疗的 CHB 相关肝硬化患者,并在入组时测量了血清病毒标记物。
elements_zh.methods: 在入组时测量了血清 HBV RNA、HBcrAg 和 HBsAg 水平,并通过多变量回归确定了 HBV RNA 阳性和 HCC 发展的预测因子。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 451 名患者中,经过中位 6.2 年的治疗后,中位 HBV RNA、HBcrAg 和 HBsAg 水平分别为 0.9 log10 拷贝/mL、3.2 log10 U/mL 和 2.4 log10 IU/mL;55 名患者在中位 3.3 年的随访期间发展为 HCC,多变量分析显示,较高的 FIB-4 指数和升高的 AFP 独立预测 HCC,而三种病毒标志物则不然。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,6 年 HBV RNA、HBcrAg 和 HBsAg 水平并不能预测接受长期恩替卡韦治疗的 CHB 相关肝硬化患者的 HCC 风险,强调了 FIB-4 和 AFP 作为预测因子的持续相关性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,常规监测 HBV RNA、HBcrAg 和 HBsAg 可能无法改善该人群的 HCC 风险预测,支持继续依赖已建立的临床和实验室标志物。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到观察设计和单一国家背景的限制,这可能会限制普遍性,并且由于缺乏针对特定目标的随机比较和潜在的残留混杂因素,证据被评估为中等。
